910.name: Early Peoples: Bubi and Pygmy Inhabitants
910.label: Event
910.description: Bubi people settle the island of Bioko (Fernando Pó) from the mainland; Pygmy communities inhabit the continental rainforest (Río Muni).

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

910.name: Bubi Settlement of Bioko
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking Bubi people migrate to Bioko island from the Cameroon coast; develop distinct culture, yam agriculture, and chieftaincy system isolated from the mainland.

910.name: Pygmy Forest Peoples of Río Muni
910.label: Event
910.description: BaKa and other Pygmy groups inhabit the equatorial rainforest of the continental region; hunter-gatherer economy; later displaced by Fang migration.

920.name: Fang Migration into Río Muni
920.label: Event
920.description: The Fang people migrate southward into the continental territory (Río Muni); warrior culture and decentralised clan-based society.

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

920.name: Fang Expansion and Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Fang clans migrate from the Sanaga River region (Cameroon) southward through the equatorial forest; displace or absorb earlier inhabitants; establish village-based chiefdoms.

920.name: Fang Social Organisation and Bieri
920.label: Event
920.description: Fang develop elaborate ancestor worship (Bieri reliquary figures); segmentary lineage system; long-distance trade in ivory and forest products.

930.name: Portuguese Discovery and Early European Contact
930.label: Event
930.description: Portuguese navigator Fernão do Pó discovers Bioko 1471; island used for slave trade; Treaty of El Pardo transfers territories to Spain.

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

930.name: Discovery of Fernando Pó
930.label: Event
930.description: Fernão do Pó reaches the island 1471; Portuguese establish limited presence; sugar plantations attempted; Bubi resist colonisation.

930.name: Treaty of El Pardo (1778)
930.label: Event
930.description: Portugal cedes Fernando Pó and Annobón to Spain in exchange for South American territories; Spain largely neglects the islands initially.

940.name: Spanish Guinea (1843–1968)
940.label: Event
940.description: Spain establishes effective control; British anti-slavery base at Clarence (Malabo); cocoa plantations with contract labour; Río Muni acquired; decolonisation.

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

940.name: British Anti-Slavery Base and Clarence
940.label: Event
940.description: Britain leases Fernando Pó as anti-slave-trade naval base; founds Clarence (now Malabo); freed slaves (Fernandinos/Krio) settle; Spain reasserts control 1855.

940.name: Spanish Cocoa Plantation Economy
940.label: Event
940.description: Cocoa plantations dominate Fernando Pó; Bubi dispossessed; contract labourers imported from Nigeria, Liberia, and Río Muni; Fernandino Creole elite.

950.name: Macías Nguema: Reign of Terror (1968–1979)
950.label: Event
950.description: Francisco Macías Nguema establishes one of Africa's most brutal dictatorships; mass executions, forced labour, and international isolation; one-third of population flees or is killed.

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

950.name: Macías Nguema's Consolidation
950.label: Event
950.description: Macías abolishes constitution; declares himself president for life; anti-Spanish and anti-intellectual purges; Nigerian labourers expelled from cocoa plantations.

950.name: The Terror: Mass Killings and Economic Collapse
950.label: Event
950.description: Estimated 50,000–80,000 killed; education banned; churches closed; country described as 'Africa's Dachau'; economy collapses; electricity and infrastructure disintegrate.

960.name: Obiang Nguema Era (1979–Present)
960.label: Event
960.description: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo becomes the world's longest-serving non-royal head of state; oil discovery transforms economy; massive corruption and human rights abuses persist.

location.place_note: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

960.name: Obiang Pre-Oil Period
960.label: Event
960.description: Obiang maintains authoritarian control; cosmetic reforms; Spanish and French aid; cocoa economy stagnates; discovery of oil at Zafiro field 1995 transforms prospects.

960.name: Oil Boom and Kleptocracy
960.label: Event
960.description: Equatorial Guinea becomes Africa's third-richest country per capita; oil revenues captured by Obiang family; son 'Teodorín' convicted of corruption in France; vast inequality.
